measurement.installation_heading:
Position the sensing element.
Keep the complete installation accessible.
measurement.installation_text: Trace possible releases from joints, seals, hoses, drains or collection trays to the proposed sensing position. Review floor slope, barriers, normal washdown and cleaning practices. Match the sensing assembly to the actual liquid and operating conditions; locate the transmitter and its connections within their approved conditions. Keep routes clear of damage and leave practical access for inspection. Use a controlled wet test and recovery check to verify each installed point and its complete notification path.

Connect the event to your workflow.

Agree device and sensing-point identifiers and notification recipients; confirm the supported event, status and reporting behavior from the supplied documentation. Local warning, valve or machine actions need their own interface and control design.

faqHeading.title: Frequently asked questions.
faqHeading.intro: Practical answers for selecting water-detection points, choosing the connection and preparing a useful commissioning and response plan.

faqs.question: What does a wireless water leak sensor detect?
paragraphs: It monitors for water reaching the installed sensing location and makes the detected condition available to a remote monitoring system through the selected wireless connection. Position the sensing element where leaked water is expected to reach it. The sensing construction and reported states are agreed for the supplied configuration.

faqs.question: How is water leak detection different from liquid-level measurement?
paragraphs: Leak detection answers whether water has reached a selected monitoring point or sensing path. Continuous liquid-level measurement measures the height or depth of liquid in a tank or vessel. Choose the product by the operational question: unwanted water at a location, or an actual level value.

faqs.question: Which connection should I choose: LoRa, 4G or NB-IoT?
paragraphs: Choose H200 for LoRa, H300 for 4G, or H500 for NB-IoT. Confirm radio coverage, the receiving infrastructure or network subscription, the destination platform and the required reporting behaviour at the planned installation. H300-WL002A is the 4G model specified for this page.

faqs.question: Where should a water leak sensor be installed in a factory?
paragraphs: Start with likely leak sources, the route water will follow, and assets that need an early maintenance response. Typical positions include drip trays, pipe joints, pump bases, cooling skids and designated low points near equipment. Keep sensing surfaces accessible for inspection and apply the approved mounting and electrical-work rules.

faqs.question: Where does the two-pin point probe detect water?
paragraphs: It detects water reaching the installed probe location. For several collection points, plan the sensing positions around the likely water paths and confirm the required number and arrangement of point probes. Discuss route or perimeter coverage as a separate sensing design.

faqs.question: Can the sensor be used for condensate, deionized water or process liquids?
paragraphs: Select the sensing assembly for the actual liquid. Conductivity, contamination, temperature and contact materials can affect detection. For condensate, purified water, glycol mixtures or process liquids, confirm suitability with a representative liquid sample and the supplied configuration before rollout.

faqs.question: How should remote notifications be commissioned?
paragraphs: Test the water alarm, received notification and any supported recovery indication according to the supplied instructions. Record the end-to-end timing under the site's network conditions.

faqs.question: Can water leak monitoring trigger a shut-off valve or machine action?
paragraphs: If a shut-off or equipment response is needed, define it as part of the site control design. Confirm the required interface, power, control logic, fail-state behaviour and commissioning method. Agree this integration separately from the wireless monitoring function.

faqs.question: What should be checked during routine maintenance?
paragraphs: Inspect the sensing surface and expected water path for dirt, damage, moved equipment or cleaning residues. Follow the supplied cleaning instructions and repeat a controlled detection and recovery check at intervals chosen for the environment and maintenance plan.

faqs.question: What information helps you configure a water leak monitoring project?
paragraphs: Send the application, country, liquid type, likely leak points, coverage area, installation photos and quantity. Include the preferred H200 LoRa, H300 4G or H500 NB-IoT connection, platform destination, required notification path and any local control requirement. We can then review the sensing arrangement and project configuration.

applications.title: Machine-tool cooling connections
applications.description: Machine tools may have spindle cooling, water supply and water-based coolant circuits close to moving hoses and service connections. Place detection at a defined collection point outside the machining enclosure to identify unexpected liquid reaching that position. For coolant mixtures, confirm the actual formulation, contamination and sensing compatibility before selecting the configuration and arranging a representative site test.
applications.measurement: Local presence of water or a confirmed compatible water-based coolant.
applications.monitoringPoint: External cooling hose connections, service trays and floor collection points beside the machine.
applications.installation: Agree a mounting point clear of moving axes, hot surfaces and routine spray. Route and secure the sensing assembly so machine servicing remains practical, and validate detection with the actual approved fluid.
applications.projectBrief: Share the machine type, circuit fluid, likely collection point and routine cleaning method.

applications.title: Injection-moulding cooling manifolds
applications.description: Mould cooling systems contain multiple supply and return connections that are disconnected or adjusted during tool changes. A defined detection position beneath an external manifold or hose service area can help the maintenance team investigate water that escapes during production. Separate normal tool-change drainage from unexpected wetness, and associate the alert with the machine and cooling zone concerned.
applications.measurement: Water reaching the selected cooling-manifold collection area.
applications.monitoringPoint: External mould-cooling manifolds, hose connection banks and approved drip-tray low points.
applications.installation: Position the approved sensing assembly outside the mould movement area and clear of hot tooling. Keep connection access available, protect exposed routing and test the chosen point under normal production and tool-change conditions.
applications.projectBrief: Tell us the manifold layout, tool-change drainage routine and number of machines or cooling zones.

applications.title: Resistance-welding cooling stations
applications.description: Water-cooled resistance-welding equipment can have flexible cooling connections between a utility supply, controller and welding cell. Detection at an accessible service-side collection point can identify water escaping beyond the intended circuit. Link each point to the affected welding station and its maintenance team so staff can inspect the relevant cooling connection.
applications.measurement: Water present at the selected external welding-cooling service point.
applications.monitoringPoint: Cooling hose junctions, external distribution blocks and service-side collection trays.
applications.installation: Choose an approved location outside robot travel, welding spatter and electrical access zones. Secure the assembly against maintenance impacts and confirm the sensing point remains reachable without entering the operating cell.
applications.projectBrief: Provide the welding-cell cooling layout, safe service boundary and expected inspection response.

applications.title: Water-circuit production test rigs
applications.description: End-of-line test rigs may connect products repeatedly to water-filled fixtures, manifolds or quick couplings. A sensor at a defined tray or external collection point can flag water that remains outside the intended test circuit. Use the test sequence to distinguish expected draining from water that requires inspection, and identify the fixture or station in the notification.
applications.measurement: Water reaching an agreed test-rig tray or floor detection point.
applications.monitoringPoint: External fixture connections, coupling service trays and test-station collection points.
applications.installation: Select a point away from moving fixtures and intentional discharge. Make the sensing assembly accessible for cleaning, and agree how wet and dry phases of the test cycle affect notification handling.
applications.projectBrief: Share the test fluid, cycle stages, intended drainage path and station identification scheme.

applications.title: Packaging-line water service bays
applications.description: Packaging and converting lines can include water-cooled tooling, rinsing services or local water conditioning equipment beside conveyors and electrical controls. Detection at an external service bay gives the maintenance team a named location to inspect when water reaches the monitoring point. Map the sensing point to the relevant machine section and distinguish production washdown from leakage that requires maintenance attention.
applications.measurement: Local water presence at a selected packaging-equipment service point.
applications.monitoringPoint: Water-service connection bays, cooling skid bases and approved collection trays beside the line.
applications.installation: Keep the detection assembly clear of conveyors, cleaning machinery and pedestrian routes. Agree a service-side mounting position, then validate the installation against both production conditions and the site's washdown routine.
applications.projectBrief: Describe the line's water services, washdown schedule and machine sections requiring individual identification.

applications.title: Water pump and booster skids
applications.description: Pump seals, flange joints, valves and flexible connectors create several possible water-release points around a booster or transfer skid. Choose detection positions using the skid's drainage pattern rather than the pump count alone. An alert can direct the maintenance team to inspect the named skid or collection area and check the relevant seal, joint or valve.
applications.measurement: Water presence at a selected pump-skid base or drainage collection point.
applications.monitoringPoint: Skid trays, seal-area drainage routes and low points near water-pipe flange connections.
applications.installation: Place the approved sensing assembly where a small release can reach it without blocking drainage. Keep it clear of rotating equipment, service lifting paths and areas routinely wet during pump maintenance.
applications.projectBrief: Send the pump-skid layout, drainage direction and whether individual pumps or the whole skid need identification.

applications.title: Chillers and heat-exchanger stations
applications.description: Cooling-water stations combine pipe joints, strainers, valves and heat-exchanger connections within a limited service area. Local water detection can identify wetness at the selected skid or floor position and help staff inspect the relevant circuit. Distinguish cooling-water leakage from normal condensate, and confirm compatibility where glycol, treatment chemicals or another water-based mixture is present in the monitored circuit.
applications.measurement: Local water or confirmed compatible cooling-fluid presence at an external collection point.
applications.monitoringPoint: Cooling-water valve stations, exchanger connection trays and chiller service-side low points.
applications.installation: Locate the approved sensing element outside hot or cold surfaces that exceed its specified conditions. Keep insulation and drain access intact, and test the actual fluid and collection route before handover.
applications.projectBrief: Specify the cooling-fluid mixture, connection temperatures and whether condensate is normally present.

applications.title: RO and water-softening systems
applications.description: Reverse-osmosis and softening skids contain service connections that are opened during filter replacement, membrane work or valve maintenance. Place the probe outside the normal drain path to detect water reaching an unintended tray or floor area. For low-conductivity permeate, confirm the sensing method with a representative sample rather than assuming every water-detection configuration performs identically.
applications.measurement: Water presence at an agreed treatment-skid collection point, using a compatible sensing method.
applications.monitoringPoint: External filter housings, membrane connection bays and skid-base collection trays.
applications.installation: Agree detection positions around the normal drain route and service clearances. Confirm the expected water conductivity, temperature and cleaning conditions, then validate response with samples from the actual monitored circuit.
applications.projectBrief: Tell us whether the monitored stream is feed water, softened water, permeate or another treatment stream.

applications.title: Boiler makeup-water service areas
applications.description: Boiler installations often have makeup-water treatment, supply valves and external service pipework around the main plant. Water detection can be specified for an accessible, suitably tempered collection position within these auxiliary areas. Identify the source circuit and expected temperature before selection, and keep boiler pressure protection, steam control and other plant safeguards under their dedicated equipment and operating procedures.
applications.measurement: Water presence at a suitably tempered makeup-water collection point.
applications.monitoringPoint: Makeup-water valve areas, auxiliary treatment-skid bases and approved external drainage interfaces.
applications.installation: Use an approved collection point clear of steam releases and hot surfaces. Verify the temperature that can reach the sensor, preserve plant access and confirm compatibility with the actual makeup-water treatment.
applications.projectBrief: Provide the makeup-water layout, potential release temperature and the proposed safe collection point.

applications.title: Compressor condensate collection
applications.description: Compressed-air systems collect condensate through drains, separators and treatment units. Detection outside the intended collection path can help identify an overflowing receiver tray or disconnected drain route that needs inspection. Confirm the condensate composition and sensing compatibility, especially where oil carryover or treatment residues may occur, and distinguish this local wetness task from monitoring the compressed-air system itself.
applications.measurement: Compatible water-based condensate reaching an unintended external collection position.
applications.monitoringPoint: Condensate treatment unit bases, drain receiver trays and external hose collection points.
applications.installation: Choose an accessible position away from pressurised air outlets and moving equipment. Assess the actual condensate before selection, keep disposal routes clear and include inspection and cleaning in the maintenance routine.
applications.projectBrief: Share the compressor type, condensate treatment arrangement and known oil or chemical content.

applications.title: Switchgear-room water ingress
applications.description: Water may reach a switchgear room through nearby services, door thresholds or building penetrations before it is obvious from the normal access route. Place detection at an approved floor position along the expected water path and give the point a clear room or board reference. The facility's electrical team defines the inspection boundary and the action to take after notification.
applications.measurement: Water reaching a selected switchgear-room perimeter detection point.
applications.monitoringPoint: Approved doorway low points, external wall interfaces and accessible floor routes outside equipment clearances.
applications.installation: Agree installation with the responsible electrical team. Keep sensing components and routing outside required access clearances and energised compartments, using approved fixing and maintenance procedures for the chosen room location.

applications.title: UPS-room external water routes
applications.description: UPS rooms can be exposed to water from cooling equipment, adjacent plant rooms or building services. A floor detection point can identify water entering an agreed external route near the room perimeter. Define this as building-water monitoring when specifying the project; battery electrolyte, battery condition and internal electrical protection require their own separately selected monitoring methods and equipment.
applications.measurement: Building-service water present at a selected UPS-room floor point.
applications.monitoringPoint: Cooling-service interfaces, room thresholds and approved floor low points outside UPS equipment.
applications.installation: Use locations approved by the facility and electrical teams. Preserve cabinet access and cable clearances, assess the installation environment and position the sensing assembly on the anticipated external water path.

applications.title: Motor-control and automation rooms
applications.description: Motor-control and automation rooms may sit beside wet production areas or receive services through shared walls and floor penetrations. Detection at an approved entrance or service-side low point can make unexpected water visible to the maintenance team through a named alert. Use the actual floor gradient and room boundary to select points, rather than placing sensors inside control cabinets by default.
applications.measurement: Water present at a selected automation-room boundary or floor route.
applications.monitoringPoint: Wet-area thresholds, service penetrations and accessible perimeter low points.
applications.installation: Agree the position with the control-room owner and electrical team. Protect the installation from carts and cleaning equipment, preserve access routes and confirm which normal cleaning events should produce a notification.

applications.title: Cable-trench water collection
applications.description: Cable trenches can collect water at low sections, duct entries or drainage interfaces that are hidden from everyday view. An approved detection point can report local water presence at a named trench section and guide an inspection. Check access, existing drainage and electrical working rules before choosing the installation; a reading describes the selected point rather than the condition of every cable route.
applications.measurement: Water reaching the selected trench low point or duct-entry collection area.
applications.monitoringPoint: Accessible trench sumps, drainage interfaces and approved low sections near duct entries.
applications.installation: Follow the site's electrical access and permit procedures. Fix the approved sensing assembly clear of cable supports and drainage paths, and arrange a maintainable route for inspection without disturbing installed circuits.

applications.title: Power-conversion plant rooms
applications.description: Inverter and power-conversion rooms can share a building envelope with water services, cooling circuits and outdoor cable entries. Local water detection at an approved floor or penetration interface helps identify which part of the room needs inspection. Separate equipment cooling-water concerns from rain ingress when mapping the points, and assign each alert to the facility team responsible for that route.
applications.measurement: Local water presence at a selected plant-room floor or entry interface.
applications.monitoringPoint: Approved cooling-service boundaries, external cable entry interfaces and room perimeter low points.
applications.installation: Select positions with the equipment owner and electrical team. Keep the sensing assembly outside energised equipment, preserve ventilation and service access, and confirm the environmental conditions of the approved detection location.

applications.title: CRAH cooling-unit service areas
applications.description: Chilled-water CRAH units combine water connections and condensate handling close to critical IT spaces. Place detection at selected valve-service or external collection positions to identify water outside the intended cooling and drainage routes. Name each point by the cooling unit and service side, so facilities staff can inspect the relevant connection or drain without treating every alert as a general room event.
applications.measurement: Water present at a selected CRAH connection or external collection point.
